_: ONE table, read by both halves of the standup's model reading (docs/modules/solitaire-agile.md): an object of named sections, each a list of rows with a name. lookup asks the model object -- Scripts/Get-PromptFileStatus.ps1 Get-P20ModelObject (tkTestToolkit -Rituals) and agent/core/models.py model_object() (Tests/test_rituals.py) -- for an id and a session id. expected null is no object: an empty or missing id, or an id of consts.json models.notModels, is not a model, known or unknown. Otherwise the object is {id, sessionId, name, family, known}: id is the row's id as written, sessionId the row's sessionId (null when the row has none or it is empty). A row whose expected.known is true takes name and family from the shipped model map's OWN row for the id (Config/models.json, consts.json models.file), so the table does not move when a row is added or a name is changed; both suites first assert the id has a row there, and a row with retired true also asserts that the map's current block names some other id for its family. A row whose expected.known is false states name and family outright: the id as written and null, because an id is looked up and never parsed -- the ids are made up, and both suites assert the map has no row for them, so a model added later cannot collide with one. An id is matched exactly, case and all, as the map lookup (Get-P20ModelInfo, model_info) matches it today. If the two halves ever disagree about a row, one of them is wrong.

another provider's known id, from its own row

a missing id is not a model

_sessions: The session reader's four sections, read by Scripts/Standup-Rules.ps1 Read-P20StandupSessions and its rules (tkTestToolkit -Rituals) and agent/solitaire/sessions.py (Tests/test_rituals.py). inside drives the pure path rule (Test-P20PathInside, path_inside): a cwd and roots in, true or false out -- separators either way, a Windows root (a drive letter, or a share) compared ignoring case and any other root ordinal, and a folder that only shares a root's name as a prefix is not inside. porcelain drives the pure parse of `git worktree list --porcelain` (ConvertFrom-P20WorktreePorcelain, parse_worktree_porcelain): the text in, the working folders out in its order, a bare entry left out. sessions is a scratch Claude Code projects folder per row: files maps a path under the projects folder to its lines, or to { mtime, lines } where mtime is the file's last write as a UTC instant (each suite sets it after writing: [System.IO.File]::SetLastWriteTimeUtc, os.utime); with no mtime a file is last written at the row's asOf. A line is a SPEC in the style of Tests/fixtures/usage/cases.json, rendered by each suite into a Claude Code line: t is the line's timestamp, written as given; sid its sessionId (left out when absent); cwd its working folder (left out when absent); model message.model; type the line's type (assistant when absent); side the subagent flag; raw a line written as it is. Every rendered line carries the content text below as its message text, so privacy can look for it. The roots are the row's checkout, then its worktrees, then the folders its porcelain text lists (the parse above), and the reader runs over [window.since, window.asOf]. expected is every {id, sessionId} pair, in the reader's order: by id, then by sessionId, ordinal. privacy holds rules every sessions row's output must meet: keys, the only keys a pair may carry; strings, no needle and no path segment (four characters or more) of the row's checkout, worktrees, porcelain folders, cwd values or project folder names (each also split on '-') anywhere in the output, ignoring case -- and both suites first assert that no such string is part of an expected id or sessionId, so the check cannot pass by accident.
content: a prompt the reader must never keep
